feu.definition:
n. A free and gratuitous right to lands made to one for service
   to be performed by him; a tenure where the vassal, in place of military
   services, makes a return in grain or in money.
feu.translation: n. 永久租借, 封地

feu de joie.definition:
A fire kindled in a public place in token of joy; a
   bonfire; a firing of guns in token of joy.
feu de joie.translation: n. <法>大篝火,鸣枪礼(士兵列队依次鸣枪以庆胜利等)

feucht.translation: [人名] 福伊希特; [地名] [德国] 福伊希特

feud.definition:
n. a bitter quarrel between two parties
v. carry out a feud
feud.translation:
n. 不和, 封地, 争执
vi. 长期不和, 擦亮

feudal.definition: a. of or relating to or characteristic of feudalism
feudal.translation: a. 封建制度的, 封地的, 领地的

feudalism.definition: n. the social system that developed in Europe in the 8th century; vassals were protected by lords who they had to serve in war
feudalism.translation: n. 封建主义, 封建制度

feudalist.translation:
n. 封建主义者
[法] 封建论者, 精通封建法的学者

feudalistic.definition: a of or relating to or characteristic of feudalism
feudalistic.translation: a. 封建制度的, 封建性的

feudalists.definition:
plural of feudalist
n. An upholder of feudalism.
feudalists.translation:
(feudalist 的复数) n. 封建主义者
[法] 封建论者, 精通封建法的学者

feudality.definition:
n. The state or quality of being feudal; feudal form or
   constitution.
feudality.translation:
n. 封建制度, 封建领地, 封地
[法] 封建制度, 封建政体, 封地

feudalization.translation: n. 形成封建制度, 封建化

feudalize.definition: v. bring (a country or people) under feudalism

feudalized.translation: v. 使成封建制度, 使封建化( feudalize的过去式和过去分词 )

feudalizes.definition: v bring (a country or people) under feudalism
feudalizes.translation: v. 使成封建制度, 使封建化( feudalize的第三人称单数 )

feudalizing.definition: p. pr. & vb. n. of Feudalize
feudalizing.translation: v. 使成封建制度, 使封建化( feudalize的现在分词 )

feudary.definition:
a. Held by, or pertaining to, feudal tenure.
n. A tenant who holds his lands by feudal service; a
   feudatory.
n. A feodary. See Feodary.
feudary.translation: n. 封建领主, 封地

feudatories.translation: n. 封臣, 封地( feudatory的名词复数 )

feudatory.definition:
a. of or pertaining to the relation of a feudal vassal to his lord
s. owing feudal allegiance to or being subject to a sovereign
feudatory.translation:
a. 受有封地的, 封地的, 封臣的
n. 封臣, 封地

feuded.translation: vi. 长期不和（feud的过去式与过去分词形式）

feudel law.translation: [法] 封建法律, 封建法

feuding.translation: vi. 长期不和（feud的现在分词形式）

feudist.definition: n. A writer on feuds; a person versed in feudal law.
feudist.translation:
n. 结下世仇的人, 封建法学家
[法] 封建主义者, 研究封建制的学者, 封建法学家

feuds.definition:
n a bitter quarrel between two parties
v carry out a feud
feuds.translation: n. 长期不和, 世仇( feud的名词复数 )

feuerbach.translation: 费尔巴哈(L.A., 1804-1872, 德国哲学家)

feuillants.definition:
n. pl. A reformed branch of the Bernardines, founded in
   1577 at Feuillans, near Toulouse, in France.
feuillants.translation: n. 费洋社（法国的政治会社）

feuille.translation:
n. 树叶味
n. (Feuille)人名；(法)弗耶

feuilles.translation:
(feuille 的复数) n. 树叶味
n. (Feuille)人名；(法)弗耶

feuilleton.definition:
n. A part of a French newspaper (usually the bottom of the
   page), devoted to light literature, criticism, etc.; also, the article
   or tale itself, thus printed.
feuilleton.translation: n. <法>报纸下面的专栏, 小品

feuilletonism.translation: n. （法）专栏副刊；小品文 (feuilleton的变形)

feuilletonist.translation: n. (欧洲报刊的)通俗文艺栏(或小品栏)作家,连载小说作家,通俗小说作家

feulgen.translation: reaction [化]福尔根反应(染色反应, 可证明细胞中染色质的存在)

feulgen method staining.translation: [医] 福侯耳根氏染色法(检染色质和去过氧核糖核酸)

feulgen reaction.translation:
[化] 福尔根氏反应
[医] 福伊耳根氏反应(试验)(检脱氧核糖核酸)

feulgen's tests.translation: [医] 福伊耳根氏试验(检脱氧核糖核酸)
